## Batch 107 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 107 brings 10 master broadcasts into canonical chronological alignment, spanning wartime combat literature, historic studio bloopers and uncensored outtakes, hot jazz classics, military morale programs, and civic political addresses: NBC's landmark ***Words at War*** special broadcast on D-Day (June 6, 1944) dramatizing beloved war correspondent Ernie Pyle's frontline tribute *Here Is Your War*, rare surviving studio master outtake reels capturing William Conrad and producer-director Norman Macdonnell breaking character during rehearsal slates for ***Gunsmoke*** (1955), Jim and Marian Jordan flubbing lines in an uncensored studio recording of ***Fibber McGee and Molly*** (1947), New Orleans soprano saxophone pioneer Sidney Bechet performing 'Muskrat Ramble' on ***The All-Time Jukebox*** hosted by Martha Wilkerson ('GI Jill') for Allied troops (1945), comedy chanteuse Cass Daley cutting exclusive AFRS tracks for *Personal Album* (1946), Harry James' trumpet solos pressed on War Department V-Discs for overseas GI listening (1944), and Academy Award-winning actor Charles Coburn lecturing on constitutional law and judicial integrity for the *Committee on Constructive Government* (1950).
